Recommendations: 1) To National Incident Commander—recommended to authorize staging of the third mission-ready mobile clinic to a Central River Basin forward hub within 6 hours (permit rotary/airlift contingency if ground routes are restricted) with a standing trigger to re-task to NE if localized conditions or shelter surge re-emerge; 2) To Public Health Operations Desk—recommended to finalize clinic staffing/manifest for the third clinic within 2 hours and prepare rapid re-deployment plans for a NE contingency; 3) To Infrastructure and Logistics Desk—recommended to concentrate remaining telecom assessment teams on highest-risk rural Central communities within 4 hours and implement temporary SATCOM/alternate comms for critical 911/coordination nodes immediately; 4) To National Logistics Center—recommended to prioritize limited fuel distribution to ambulances, shelter/generator sites and critical telecom nodes in the Central Basin and hold a small reserve for NE patient-transport needs if requested; 5) To Air Operations Liaison—recommended to allocate remaining rotary-wing hours to NE highest-priority patient transfers while preserving minimal sortie capacity for time-critical Central resupply/evacuations, with manifests coordinated within 2 hours.  
Rationale and Assumptions: Recommendations prioritize Central staging because of concentrated residual risk and persistent rural comms gaps, assume current asset, fuel and air-hour reports are accurate but preliminary/unconfirmed, and recognize these provisional taskings must be adjusted rapidly if road access, weather, or asset availability changes.
